title: John Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 10.

questions.question: In John 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: He that entereth not by the door
questions.correctAnswer: He that entereth not by the door
questions.explanation: This statement appears in John 10:1, making it the first event in the chapter.

questions.question: Who is referred to as the shepherd of the sheep in John 10?
options: He that entereth by the door
questions.correctAnswer: He that entereth by the door
questions.explanation: John 10:2 states that he who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.

questions.question: What do the sheep do when they hear the voice of their shepherd?
questions.explanation: According to John 10:4, the sheep follow the shepherd because they know his voice.

questions.question: What will the sheep not do regarding a stranger?
questions.explanation: John 10:5 indicates that the sheep will not follow a stranger but will flee from him.

questions.question: What did Jesus say he is in John 10?
questions.explanation: In John 10:7, Jesus states, 'I am the door of the sheep.'

questions.question: What did Jesus come to provide according to John 10:10?
questions.explanation: John 10:10 states that Jesus came that they might have life and have it more abundantly.

questions.question: What does the good shepherd do for the sheep?
options: Gives his life for the sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Gives his life for the sheep
questions.explanation: John 10:11 states that the good shepherd gives his life for the sheep.

questions.question: What happens when the hireling sees the wolf coming?
questions.explanation: John 10:12 indicates that the hireling sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep.

questions.question: How do the sheep know the good shepherd?
questions.explanation: According to John 10:4, the sheep follow him because they know his voice.

questions.question: Who does the porter open for?
questions.explanation: John 10:3 states that the porter openeth to him, which refers to the shepherd.

questions.question: The sheep did not hear whom according to John 10:8?
questions.explanation: John 10:8 mentions that all who came before Jesus are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said he is the good shepherd.
questions.explanation: In John 10:11, Jesus explicitly states, 'I am the good shepherd.'

questions.question: True or False: The hireling cares deeply for the sheep.
questions.explanation: John 10:13 states that the hireling flees because he is an hireling and cares not for the sheep.

questions.question: True or False: The good shepherd flees when danger comes.
questions.explanation: This is false as the good shepherd does not flee; he gives his life for the sheep (John 10:11).

questions.question: True or False: The sheep follow the wolf.
questions.explanation: This is false as John 10:5 states that the sheep will not follow a stranger but will flee from him.

medium.title: John Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Jesus say He does for the sheep?
options: I lay down my life for the sheep.
I lead them to green pastures.
questions.correctAnswer: I lay down my life for the sheep.
questions.explanation: This is stated in John 10:15, where Jesus emphasizes His sacrificial love for His followers.

questions.question: What does John 10:16 promise will happen if someone hears the voice of Jesus?
options: They shall be part of one fold with one shepherd.
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be part of one fold with one shepherd.
questions.explanation: In John 10:16, Jesus speaks about bringing other sheep into one fold, indicating unity and belonging.

questions.question: Why does the Father love Jesus according to John 10:17?
options: Because He lays down His life.
questions.correctAnswer: Because He lays down His life.
questions.explanation: John 10:17 explains that the Father loves Jesus specifically for His willingness to sacrifice His life for others.

questions.question: If someone believes in Jesus, what does John 10:28 assure them?
options: They will always follow the shepherd.
questions.explanation: John 10:28 guarantees that those who are His sheep will have eternal life and will not be lost.

questions.question: What is the consequence of not believing in Jesus according to John 10:26?
options: They will not be part of His sheep.
questions.correctAnswer: They will not be part of His sheep.
questions.explanation: John 10:26 indicates that disbelief is a barrier to being recognized as one of Jesus' sheep.

questions.question: According to John 10:20, what did many people say about Jesus?
options: He has a devil and is mad.
questions.correctAnswer: He has a devil and is mad.
questions.explanation: In John 10:20, some people accused Jesus of being possessed and mad due to His teachings.

questions.question: What do Jesus' works bear witness to according to John 10:25?
questions.explanation: Jesus states in John 10:25 that His works, done in His Father's name, testify about who He truly is.

questions.question: What do the sheep do according to John 10:27?
questions.explanation: In John 10:27, Jesus describes how His sheep recognize His voice and follow Him.

questions.question: What does John 10:19 reveal about the reaction of the Jews to Jesus' teachings?
questions.explanation: John 10:19 indicates that Jesus' words caused division among the Jews, reflecting mixed reactions.

questions.question: What is the role of the good shepherd according to John 10:11?
options: To lead the sheep to safety.
To give his life for the sheep.
To protect the sheep from thieves.
questions.correctAnswer: To give his life for the sheep.
questions.explanation: John 10:11 explicitly states that the good shepherd sacrifices himself for the sake of the sheep.

questions.question: According to John 10:24, what did the Jews ask Jesus?
options: If He was the Son of God.
If He could heal the sick.
If He would free them from Rome.
questions.explanation: John 10:24 shows that the Jews were looking for a clear declaration of Jesus' identity as the Messiah.

questions.question: What does John 10:22 state about the setting of Jesus' teachings?
options: It was during the Feast of Dedication.
It was in a private house.
questions.correctAnswer: It was during the Feast of Dedication.
questions.explanation: John 10:22 specifically states that Jesus was teaching during the Feast of Dedication in winter.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus has the power to lay down His life and take it again?
questions.explanation: John 10:18 affirms that Jesus has the authority to lay down His life and take it back, which is a testament to His divine power.

questions.question: Is it false that Jesus' sheep do not hear His voice?
questions.explanation: John 10:27 clearly states that Jesus' sheep hear His voice, indicating a relationship of recognition and trust.

questions.question: Is it false that Jesus is the door of the sheep?
questions.explanation: In John 10:7, Jesus identifies Himself as the door of the sheep, meaning He is the way to safety and salvation.

hard.title: John Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 10.

questions.question: What did Jesus claim about the relationship between Him and the Father?
options: The Father is greater than Him
questions.explanation: This is stated in John 10:30 where Jesus says, 'I and my Father are one.' This indicates a unique unity between Jesus and the Father.

questions.question: Why did the Jews seek to stone Jesus?
questions.explanation: The Jews answered in John 10:33, stating, 'For a good work we stone thee not; but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.'

questions.question: What works does Jesus ask the Jews to believe in?
questions.explanation: In John 10:37, Jesus says, 'If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not.' He points to His works as evidence of His divine authority.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about those who hear His voice?
questions.explanation: In John 10:27, Jesus states, 'My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me,' indicating the intimate relationship between Him and His followers.

questions.question: What is promised to Jesus' sheep?
questions.explanation: In John 10:28, Jesus promises, 'And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish...' showing the assurance of salvation for His followers.

questions.question: What commandment did Jesus say He received from the Father?
options: To lay down and take up His life
questions.correctAnswer: To lay down and take up His life
questions.explanation: In John 10:18, Jesus explains, 'I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ποιμήν' (poimēn) in John 10:11 mean?
questions.explanation: 'ποιμήν' is the Greek word for 'shepherd,' which is used in John 10:11 where Jesus identifies Himself as 'the good shepherd.'

questions.question: What literary device is employed in the phrase 'I am the good shepherd'?
questions.explanation: Jesus uses a metaphor in John 10:11 by referring to Himself as 'the good shepherd,' illustrating His role as a protector and caretaker of His followers.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse connects to the theme of Jesus as the shepherd?
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:1 states, 'The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want,' which connects to the theme in John 10 where Jesus proclaims Himself as the shepherd.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage affirms that believers cannot be snatched from God's hand?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:38-39 affirms that nothing can separate us from the love of God, echoing the assurance in John 10:29 that no one can pluck them out of the Father's hand.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Jesus declares that He and the Father are one?
options: He states that His sheep hear His voice
questions.explanation: In John 10:31, it is stated that 'Then the Jews took up stones again to stone him,' which sets the context for His declaration in John 10:30.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the scripture cannot be broken' imply in John 10:35?
questions.explanation: In John 10:35, Jesus affirms the authority of scripture, stating that it cannot be broken, highlighting its eternal truth and reliability.

questions.question: The statement 'I lay down my life for the sheep' shows what aspect of Jesus' character?
questions.explanation: In John 10:11, Jesus declares, 'the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep,' illustrating His willingness to sacrifice for the sake of His followers.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus claimed to be the door of the sheep?
questions.explanation: In John 10:7, Jesus explicitly states, 'I am the door of the sheep,' indicating His role as the entrance to salvation.

questions.question: Is it false that the Jews believed Jesus was mad?
questions.explanation: In John 10:20, it is noted that 'many of them said, He hath a devil, and is mad,' indicating that some indeed believed He was mad.

theological.title: John Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 10:9 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is found only through Jesus, the door to the sheepfold
Salvation comes through strict adherence to the law
Salvation depends on human effort to enter the sheepfold
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is found only through Jesus, the door to the sheepfold
questions.explanation: John 10:9 states, 'I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved,' teaching that salvation is exclusively through Jesus as the entry point.

questions.question: What doctrine about the identity of Christ is presented in John 10:30?
options: Jesus and the Father are one in essence and purpose
Jesus is subordinate to the Father
Jesus is merely a prophet sent by God
Jesus and the Father are two separate gods
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus and the Father are one in essence and purpose
questions.explanation: John 10:30 says, 'I and my Father are one,' affirming the unity of essence and purpose between Jesus and the Father, a foundational Trinitarian doctrine.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ’s atoning work is taught in John 10:11?
options: Jesus, the good shepherd, lays down his life for the sheep
Jesus offers a symbolic sacrifice only
Jesus does not die but teaches about life
Jesus’ death is incidental and not redemptive
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus, the good shepherd, lays down his life for the sheep
questions.explanation: John 10:11 states, 'the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep,' teaching the doctrine of Christ’s sacrificial atonement for his people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 10:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: John 10:14 says, 'I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep,' showing Jesus’ omniscience in knowing each believer intimately.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in John 10:29 concerning the security of believers?
questions.explanation: John 10:29 states, 'My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand,' emphasizing God’s sovereign power to protect believers.

questions.question: How does John 10 prepare for the fulfillment of Old Testament Messianic expectations?
options: By presenting Jesus as the shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep
By emphasizing the need for temple sacrifices
By detailing the Mosaic Law for Israel
By focusing on political liberation from Rome
questions.correctAnswer: By presenting Jesus as the shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep
questions.explanation: John 10’s imagery of Jesus as the good shepherd fulfills Old Testament prophecies (e.g., Ezekiel 34) about the Messiah’s care and sacrificial role for Israel.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does John 10:16 make regarding Gentile inclusion?
options: Christ will bring other sheep not of this fold to form one flock
The covenant is renewed exclusively with ethnic Israel
Salvation is limited to the Jewish people
The Gentiles must become Jews to be saved
questions.correctAnswer: Christ will bring other sheep not of this fold to form one flock
questions.explanation: John 10:16 teaches that Jesus has other sheep not of the Jewish fold whom he must bring in, indicating the inclusion of Gentiles into one flock under one shepherd.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 10:27 and John 10:28 teach about the security and knowledge of believers?
options: The sheep hear and know the shepherd’s voice, and are given eternal life guaranteeing their security
Believers must continually prove their faith to remain saved
The sheep are only temporarily secured and can be lost
Salvation depends on human effort to follow the voice
questions.correctAnswer: The sheep hear and know the shepherd’s voice, and are given eternal life guaranteeing their security
questions.explanation: John 10:27-28 describe the intimate knowledge between Jesus and his sheep, who hear his voice and follow him, and that he gives them eternal life that cannot be lost, affirming eternal security.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 10:15 and John 10:18 teach about Christ’s authority over life and death?
options: Jesus lays down his life voluntarily and has power to take it up again by divine authority
Jesus’ death was forced upon him without his consent
Jesus cannot control his own life or death
Jesus’ resurrection is uncertain and dependent on human intervention
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus lays down his life voluntarily and has power to take it up again by divine authority
questions.explanation: John 10:15 and 10:18 both affirm that Jesus lays down his life willingly and has the divine power to take it up again, showing his sovereign authority over life and death.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 10:33 and John 10:36 teach about the Sonship and divinity of Christ?
options: Jesus claims to be the Son of God, and this claim is understood as blasphemy by the Jews because it asserts his divinity
Jesus denies any divine status and claims only to be a man
The Jews accept Jesus as God without objection
Jesus claims to be a prophet but not divine
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus claims to be the Son of God, and this claim is understood as blasphemy by the Jews because it asserts his divinity
questions.explanation: John 10:33 and 36 show the Jews accusing Jesus of blasphemy for making himself God by claiming to be the Son of God, affirming the doctrine of Christ’s divine Sonship.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jesus’ statement in John 10:30 implies he is not truly divine. What does John 10:30-33 actually teach?
options: Jesus declares unity with the Father, which the Jews interpret as a blasphemous claim to deity
Jesus claims to be a separate god alongside the Father
Jesus denies divinity and only claims close friendship with God
Jesus speaks metaphorically without real divine unity
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus declares unity with the Father, which the Jews interpret as a blasphemous claim to deity
questions.explanation: John 10:30-33 records Jesus’ statement 'I and my Father are one' and the Jews’ reaction accusing him of blasphemy, showing the claim of divine unity and deity.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of false teachers is taught in John 10:1-2?
options: Those who do not enter by the door are thieves and robbers, contrasting with the true shepherd who enters rightly
All teachers are equally valid paths to God
False teachers are not mentioned in this passage
Anyone who climbs into the sheepfold is welcomed as a shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: Those who do not enter by the door are thieves and robbers, contrasting with the true shepherd who enters rightly
questions.explanation: John 10:1-2 contrasts true shepherds who enter by the door with thieves and robbers who climb in another way, teaching a doctrine about the illegitimacy of false teachers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily demonstrated in John 10:17 regarding the love of the Father?
questions.explanation: John 10:17 states, 'Therefore doth my Father love me,' explicitly showing the attribute of divine love between Father and Son.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is reflected in John 10:24-25 concerning Jesus’ identity and the response of the Jews?
options: The tension between Jesus’ messianic claims and Jewish rejection
The immediate acceptance of Jesus as Messiah by all Jews
The focus on political revolution against Rome
The endorsement of Jesus by the Sanhedrin
questions.correctAnswer: The tension between Jesus’ messianic claims and Jewish rejection
questions.explanation: John 10:24-25 shows Jews challenging Jesus to declare plainly if he is the Christ, revealing the tension and rejection that characterize Jesus’ messianic mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the nature of Jesus’ works and divine endorsement is taught in John 10:25 and John 10:38?
options: Jesus’ works bear witness to his identity and reveal the Father’s presence in him
Jesus’ works are meaningless without human belief
Jesus performs miracles through demonic power
Jesus denies that his works have any divine origin
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ works bear witness to his identity and reveal the Father’s presence in him
questions.explanation: John 10:25 and 10:38 emphasize that Jesus’ works testify to his divine mission and the indwelling Father, calling for belief based on the evidence of miracles.
